blocks.source: Canto XXVIII
blocks.translation: Canto XXVIII

blocks.source: Chi poria mai pur con parole sciolte
blocks.translation: Who ever could, e’en with untrammelled words,

blocks.source: dicer del sangue e de le piaghe a pieno
blocks.translation: Tell of the blood and of the wounds in full

blocks.source: ch’i’ ora vidi, per narrar più volte?
blocks.translation: Which now I saw, by many times narrating?

blocks.source: Ogne lingua per certo verria meno
blocks.translation: Each tongue would for a certainty fall short

blocks.source: per lo nostro sermone e per la mente
blocks.translation: By reason of our speech and memory,

blocks.source: c’hanno a tanto comprender poco seno.
blocks.translation: That have small room to comprehend so much.

blocks.source: S’el s’aunasse ancor tutta la gente
blocks.translation: If were again assembled all the people

blocks.source: che già, in su la fortunata terra
blocks.translation: Which formerly upon the fateful land

blocks.source: di Puglia, fu del suo sangue dolente
blocks.translation: Of Puglia were lamenting for their blood

blocks.source: per li Troiani e per la lunga guerra
blocks.translation: Shed by the Romans and the lingering war

blocks.source: che de l’anella fé sì alte spoglie,
blocks.translation: That of the rings made such illustrious spoils,

blocks.source: come Livïo scrive, che non erra,
blocks.translation: As Livy has recorded, who errs not,

blocks.source: con quella che sentio di colpi doglie
blocks.translation: With those who felt the agony of blows

blocks.source: per contastare a Ruberto Guiscardo;
blocks.translation: By making counterstand to Robert Guiscard,

blocks.source: e l’altra il cui ossame ancor s’accoglie
blocks.translation: And all the rest, whose bones are gathered still

blocks.source: a Ceperan, là dove fu bugiardo
blocks.translation: At Ceperano, where a renegade

blocks.source: ciascun Pugliese, e là da Tagliacozzo,
blocks.translation: Was each Apulian, and at Tagliacozzo,

blocks.source: dove sanz’ arme vinse il vecchio Alardo;
blocks.translation: Where without arms the old Alardo conquered,

blocks.source: e qual forato suo membro e qual mozzo
blocks.translation: And one his limb transpierced, and one lopped off,

blocks.source: mostrasse, d’aequar sarebbe nulla
blocks.translation: Should show, it would be nothing to compare

blocks.source: il modo de la nona bolgia sozzo.
blocks.translation: With the disgusting mode of the ninth Bolgia.

blocks.source: Già veggia, per mezzul perdere o lulla,
blocks.translation: A cask by losing centre-piece or cant

blocks.source: com’ io vidi un, così non si pertugia,
blocks.translation: Was never shattered so, as I saw one

blocks.source: rotto dal mento infin dove si trulla.
blocks.translation: Rent from the chin to where one breaketh wind.

blocks.source: Tra le gambe pendevan le minugia;
blocks.translation: Between his legs were hanging down his entrails;

blocks.source: la corata pareva e ’l tristo sacco
blocks.translation: His heart was visible, and the dismal sack

blocks.source: che merda fa di quel che si trangugia.
blocks.translation: That maketh excrement of what is eaten.

blocks.source: Mentre che tutto in lui veder m’attacco,
blocks.translation: While I was all absorbed in seeing him,

blocks.source: guardommi e con le man s’aperse il petto,
blocks.translation: He looked at me, and opened with his hands

blocks.source: dicendo: «Or vedi com’ io mi dilacco!
blocks.translation: His bosom, saying: “See now how I rend me;

blocks.source: vedi come storpiato è Mäometto!
blocks.translation: How mutilated, see, is Mahomet;

blocks.source: Dinanzi a me sen va piangendo Alì,
blocks.translation: In front of me doth Ali weeping go,

blocks.source: fesso nel volto dal mento al ciuffetto.
blocks.translation: Cleft in the face from forelock unto chin;

blocks.source: E tutti li altri che tu vedi qui,
blocks.translation: And all the others whom thou here beholdest,

blocks.source: seminator di scandalo e di scisma
blocks.translation: Disseminators of scandal and of schism

blocks.source: fuor vivi, e però son fessi così.
blocks.translation: While living were, and therefore are cleft thus.

blocks.source: Un diavolo è qua dietro che n’accisma
blocks.translation: A devil is behind here, who doth cleave us

blocks.source: sì crudelmente, al taglio de la spada
blocks.translation: Thus cruelly, unto the falchion’s edge

blocks.source: rimettendo ciascun di questa risma,
blocks.translation: Putting again each one of all this ream,

blocks.source: quand’ avem volta la dolente strada;
blocks.translation: When we have gone around the doleful road;

blocks.source: però che le ferite son richiuse
blocks.translation: By reason that our wounds are closed again

blocks.source: prima ch’altri dinanzi li rivada.
blocks.translation: Ere any one in front of him repass.

blocks.source: Ma tu chi se’ che ’n su lo scoglio muse,
blocks.translation: But who art thou, that musest on the crag,

blocks.source: forse per indugiar d’ire a la pena
blocks.translation: Perchance to postpone going to the pain

blocks.source: ch’è giudicata in su le tue accuse?».
blocks.translation: That is adjudged upon thine accusations?”

blocks.source: «Né morte ’l giunse ancor, né colpa ’l mena»,
blocks.translation: “Nor death hath reached him yet, nor guilt doth bring him,”

blocks.source: rispuose ’l mio maestro, «a tormentarlo;
blocks.translation: My Master made reply, “to be tormented;

blocks.source: ma per dar lui esperïenza piena,
blocks.translation: But to procure him full experience,

blocks.source: a me, che morto son, convien menarlo
blocks.translation: Me, who am dead, behoves it to conduct him

blocks.source: per lo ’nferno qua giù di giro in giro;
blocks.translation: Down here through Hell, from circle unto circle;

blocks.source: e quest’ è ver così com’ io ti parlo».
blocks.translation: And this is true as that I speak to thee.”

blocks.source: Più fuor di cento che, quando l’udiro,
blocks.translation: More than a hundred were there when they heard him,

blocks.source: s’arrestaron nel fosso a riguardarmi
blocks.translation: Who in the moat stood still to look at me,

blocks.source: per maraviglia, oblïando il martiro.
blocks.translation: Through wonderment oblivious of their torture.

blocks.source: «Or dì a fra Dolcin dunque che s’armi,
blocks.translation: “Now say to Fra Dolcino, then, to arm him,

blocks.source: tu che forse vedra’ il sole in breve,
blocks.translation: Thou, who perhaps wilt shortly see the sun,

blocks.source: s’ello non vuol qui tosto seguitarmi,
blocks.translation: If soon he wish not here to follow me,

blocks.source: sì di vivanda, che stretta di neve
blocks.translation: So with provisions, that no stress of snow

blocks.source: non rechi la vittoria al Noarese,
blocks.translation: May give the victory to the Novarese,

blocks.source: ch’altrimenti acquistar non saria leve».
blocks.translation: Which otherwise to gain would not be easy.”

blocks.source: Poi che l’un piè per girsene sospese,
blocks.translation: After one foot to go away he lifted,

blocks.source: Mäometto mi disse esta parola;
blocks.translation: This word did Mahomet say unto me,

blocks.source: indi a partirsi in terra lo distese.
blocks.translation: Then to depart upon the ground he stretched it.

blocks.source: Un altro, che forata avea la gola
blocks.translation: Another one, who had his throat pierced through,

blocks.source: e tronco ’l naso infin sotto le ciglia,
blocks.translation: And nose cut off close underneath the brows,

blocks.source: e non avea mai ch’una orecchia sola,
blocks.translation: And had no longer but a single ear,

blocks.source: ristato a riguardar per maraviglia
blocks.translation: Staying to look in wonder with the others,

blocks.source: con li altri, innanzi a li altri aprì la canna,
blocks.translation: Before the others did his gullet open,

blocks.source: ch’era di fuor d’ogne parte vermiglia,
blocks.translation: Which outwardly was red in every part,

blocks.source: e disse: «O tu cui colpa non condanna
blocks.translation: And said: “O thou, whom guilt doth not condemn,

blocks.source: e cu’ io vidi su in terra latina,
blocks.translation: And whom I once saw up in Latian land,

blocks.source: se troppa simiglianza non m’inganna,
blocks.translation: Unless too great similitude deceive me,

blocks.source: rimembriti di Pier da Medicina,
blocks.translation: Call to remembrance Pier da Medicina,

blocks.source: se mai torni a veder lo dolce piano
blocks.translation: If e’er thou see again the lovely plain

blocks.source: che da Vercelli a Marcabò dichina.
blocks.translation: That from Vercelli slopes to Marcabo,

blocks.source: E fa saper a’ due miglior da Fano,
blocks.translation: And make it known to the best two of Fano,

blocks.source: a messer Guido e anco ad Angiolello,
blocks.translation: To Messer Guido and Angiolello likewise,

blocks.source: che, se l’antiveder qui non è vano,
blocks.translation: That if foreseeing here be not in vain,

blocks.source: gittati saran fuor di lor vasello
blocks.translation: Cast over from their vessel shall they be,

blocks.source: e mazzerati presso a la Cattolica
blocks.translation: And drowned near unto the Cattolica,

blocks.source: per tradimento d’un tiranno fello.
blocks.translation: By the betrayal of a tyrant fell.

blocks.source: Tra l’isola di Cipri e di Maiolica
blocks.translation: Between the isles of Cyprus and Majorca

blocks.source: non vide mai sì gran fallo Nettuno,
blocks.translation: Neptune ne’er yet beheld so great a crime,

blocks.source: non da pirate, non da gente argolica.
blocks.translation: Neither of pirates nor Argolic people.

blocks.source: Quel traditor che vede pur con l’uno,
blocks.translation: That traitor, who sees only with one eye,

blocks.source: e tien la terra che tale qui meco
blocks.translation: And holds the land, which some one here with me

blocks.source: vorrebbe di vedere esser digiuno,
blocks.translation: Would fain be fasting from the vision of,

blocks.source: farà venirli a parlamento seco;
blocks.translation: Will make them come unto a parley with him;

blocks.source: poi farà sì, ch’al vento di Focara
blocks.translation: Then will do so, that to Focara’s wind

blocks.source: non sarà lor mestier voto né preco».
blocks.translation: They will not stand in need of vow or prayer.”

blocks.source: E io a lui: «Dimostrami e dichiara,
blocks.translation: And I to him: “Show to me and declare,

blocks.source: se vuo’ ch’i’ porti sù di te novella,
blocks.translation: If thou wouldst have me bear up news of thee,

blocks.source: chi è colui da la veduta amara».
blocks.translation: Who is this person of the bitter vision.”

blocks.source: Allor puose la mano a la mascella
blocks.translation: Then did he lay his hand upon the jaw

blocks.source: d’un suo compagno e la bocca li aperse,
blocks.translation: Of one of his companions, and his mouth

blocks.source: gridando: «Questi è desso, e non favella.
blocks.translation: Oped, crying: “This is he, and he speaks not.

blocks.source: Questi, scacciato, il dubitar sommerse
blocks.translation: This one, being banished, every doubt submerged

blocks.source: in Cesare, affermando che ’l fornito
blocks.translation: In Caesar by affirming the forearmed

blocks.source: sempre con danno l’attender sofferse».
blocks.translation: Always with detriment allowed delay.”

blocks.source: Oh quanto mi pareva sbigottito
blocks.translation: O how bewildered unto me appeared,

blocks.source: con la lingua tagliata ne la strozza
blocks.translation: With tongue asunder in his windpipe slit,

blocks.source: Curïo, ch’a dir fu così ardito!
blocks.translation: Curio, who in speaking was so bold!

blocks.source: E un ch’avea l’una e l’altra man mozza,
blocks.translation: And one, who both his hands dissevered had,

blocks.source: levando i moncherin per l’aura fosca,
blocks.translation: The stumps uplifting through the murky air,

blocks.source: sì che ’l sangue facea la faccia sozza,
blocks.translation: So that the blood made horrible his face,

blocks.source: gridò: «Ricordera’ti anche del Mosca,
blocks.translation: Cried out: “Thou shalt remember Mosca also,

blocks.source: che disse, lasso!, “Capo ha cosa fatta”,
blocks.translation: Who said, alas! ‘A thing done has an end!’

blocks.source: che fu mal seme per la gente tosca».
blocks.translation: Which was an ill seed for the Tuscan people.”

blocks.source: E io li aggiunsi: «E morte di tua schiatta»;
blocks.translation: “And death unto thy race,” thereto I added;

blocks.source: per ch’elli, accumulando duol con duolo,
blocks.translation: Whence he, accumulating woe on woe,

blocks.source: sen gio come persona trista e matta.
blocks.translation: Departed, like a person sad and crazed.

blocks.source: Ma io rimasi a riguardar lo stuolo,
blocks.translation: But I remained to look upon the crowd;

blocks.source: e vidi cosa ch’io avrei paura,
blocks.translation: And saw a thing which I should be afraid,

blocks.source: sanza più prova, di contarla solo;
blocks.translation: Without some further proof, even to recount,

blocks.source: se non che coscïenza m’assicura,
blocks.translation: If it were not that conscience reassures me,

blocks.source: la buona compagnia che l’uom francheggia
blocks.translation: That good companion which emboldens man

blocks.source: sotto l’asbergo del sentirsi pura.
blocks.translation: Beneath the hauberk of its feeling pure.

blocks.source: Io vidi certo, e ancor par ch’io ’l veggia,
blocks.translation: I truly saw, and still I seem to see it,

blocks.source: un busto sanza capo andar sì come
blocks.translation: A trunk without a head walk in like manner

blocks.source: andavan li altri de la trista greggia;
blocks.translation: As walked the others of the mournful herd.

blocks.source: e ’l capo tronco tenea per le chiome,
blocks.translation: And by the hair it held the head dissevered,

blocks.source: pesol con mano a guisa di lanterna:
blocks.translation: Hung from the hand in fashion of a lantern,

blocks.source: e quel mirava noi e dicea: «Oh me!».
blocks.translation: And that upon us gazed and said: “O me!”

blocks.source: Di sé facea a sé stesso lucerna,
blocks.translation: It of itself made to itself a lamp,

blocks.source: ed eran due in uno e uno in due;
blocks.translation: And they were two in one, and one in two;

blocks.source: com’ esser può, quei sa che sì governa.
blocks.translation: How that can be, He knows who so ordains it.

blocks.source: Quando diritto al piè del ponte fue,
blocks.translation: When it was come close to the bridge’s foot,

blocks.source: levò ’l braccio alto con tutta la testa
blocks.translation: It lifted high its arm with all the head,

blocks.source: per appressarne le parole sue,
blocks.translation: To bring more closely unto us its words,

blocks.source: che fuoro: «Or vedi la pena molesta,
blocks.translation: Which were: “Behold now the sore penalty,

blocks.source: tu che, spirando, vai veggendo i morti:
blocks.translation: Thou, who dost breathing go the dead beholding;

blocks.source: vedi s’alcuna è grande come questa.
blocks.translation: Behold if any be as great as this.

blocks.source: E perché tu di me novella porti,
blocks.translation: And so that thou may carry news of me,

blocks.source: sappi ch’i’ son Bertram dal Bornio, quelli
blocks.translation: Know that Bertram de Born am I, the same

blocks.source: che diedi al re giovane i ma’ conforti.
blocks.translation: Who gave to the Young King the evil comfort.

blocks.source: Io feci il padre e ’l figlio in sé ribelli;
blocks.translation: I made the father and the son rebellious;

blocks.source: Achitofèl non fé più d’Absalone
blocks.translation: Achitophel not more with Absalom

blocks.source: e di Davìd coi malvagi punzelli.
blocks.translation: And David did with his accursed goadings.

blocks.source: Perch’ io parti’ così giunte persone,
blocks.translation: Because I parted persons so united,

blocks.source: partito porto il mio cerebro, lasso!,
blocks.translation: Parted do I now bear my brain, alas!

blocks.source: dal suo principio ch’è in questo troncone.
blocks.translation: From its beginning, which is in this trunk.

blocks.source: Così s’osserva in me lo contrapasso».
blocks.translation: Thus is observed in me the counterpoise.”
